discovery: Transparent amorphous oxide semiconductors (IGZO) and their thin-film transistors
subfield: Condensed matter physics / semiconductor materials and devices
motivation: Conventional wisdom held that amorphous semiconductors must have poor carrier transport, because disorder destroys the directional covalent bonds of silicon. Hideo Hosono, with Toshio Kamiya, showed from basic materials physics that this is not true for ionic oxides of heavy post-transition metals. Their conduction bands are built from large, spherical ns orbitals, which overlap strongly whatever the bond angles. From this principle they designed amorphous In-Ga-Zn-O and reported in 2004 room-temperature-fabricated, flexible, transparent thin-film transistors with mobilities more than ten times higher than amorphous silicon. IGZO transistors now drive high-resolution, low-power LCD and OLED displays in billions of phones, tablets and televisions. Their very low off-current also saves a great deal of energy. This is a model of how patient materials design, going against fashion, becomes a technology that benefits society worldwide.
